import pandas as pd

# Source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_3/training_0.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes from all sources
dfs = []

# Load each source file
for file in source_files:
    # Read CSV with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since there is only one source table, transformation is straightforward:
# Target schema: ['Major_category': string, 'Median': float]
# Source schema contains these columns, so we just select and ensure types.

# Extract relevant columns from the single source dataframe
df_source = dfs[0][['Major_category', 'Median']].copy()

# Ensure correct types
df_source['Major_category'] = df_source['Major_category'].astype(str)
df_source['Median'] = df_source['Median'].astype(float)

# According to the target examples, the target table has 9 rows.
# The source has 87 rows, so we need to aggregate by Major_category to get one Median per category.
# The target examples show Median as a single float per Major_category.
# We will compute the median of Median values per Major_category to match the target style.

df_target = df_source.groupby('Major_category', as_index=False)['Median'].median()

# Save the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_3/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
